symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of independently sampled units.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: The index for the control and treatment sides of the assignment boundary.

symbols.name: \overline\kappa
symbols.def: A fixed upper endpoint for the thickness regimes considered simultaneously.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: The exponent governing polynomial depletion of one-sided boundary-neighborhood mass.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: A fixed envelope for side-regression Lipschitz constants and boundary traces.

symbols.name: \sigma
symbols.def: A fixed known conditional sub-Gaussian proxy for the observed regression residual; in the explicit Gaussian witness submodels it is also the noise standard deviation.

symbols.name: c_{m}
symbols.def: The common lower constant in the polynomial one-sided local-mass bound.

symbols.name: C_{m}
symbols.def: The threshold constant used to classify a boundary location as polynomially thin.

symbols.name: h_0
symbols.def: The largest radius on which boundary regularity and local-mass conditions are imposed.

symbols.name: \gamma
symbols.def: The target simultaneous miscoverage probability.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The observed location or eligibility score.

symbols.name: Y(0)
symbols.def: The potential outcome under control.

symbols.name: Y(1)
symbols.def: The potential outcome under treatment.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_0
symbols.def: The known region assigned to control.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_1
symbols.def: The known region assigned to treatment.

symbols.name: T
symbols.def: \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_1\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_n
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_n=(O_i:1\le i\le n)\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A law for the potential outcomes and score that induces the observed law of \(O\).

symbols.name: P_{X}
symbols.def: \(P_X\) is the \(X\)-marginal of \(P\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B=\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_0)\cap\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_1)\).

symbols.name: d
symbols.def: \(d(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\).

symbols.name: \mathcal X_{t,P}
symbols.def: \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\), where \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\) is the one-sided restricted score measure.

symbols.name: g_{t,P}
symbols.def: \(g_{t,P}\) denotes a Borel representative on \(\mathcal X_{t,P}=\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\) of the observed-outcome regression equivalence class \(z\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=z]\) for \(z\in\mathcal A_t\), with equivalence taken under the one-sided restricted score measure. On \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\), it is the unique representative satisfying the \(L\)-Lipschitz condition imposed by the model classes.

symbols.name: \theta_{t,P}
symbols.def: \(\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)\), the unique trace on the model classes below.

symbols.name: \tau_P
symbols.def: \(\tau_P(x)=\theta_{1,P}(x)-\theta_{0,P}(x)\).

symbols.name: q_{t,P}
symbols.def: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)=P\{X\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X,x)\le h\}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf J_P
symbols.def: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) is the largest cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\{x\in\mathcal B:\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}q_{t,P}(x,h)\le u\}\).

symbols.name: K_P
symbols.def: \(K_P(x,h)=1\vee\mathsf J_P(h,a_P(x,h))\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H_n
symbols.def: \(\mathcal H_n=\{2^{-j}h_0:0\le j\le\lceil\log_2 n\rceil\}\).

symbols.name: r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}
symbols.def: The oracle benchmark constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}oracle\text{-}benchmark}\).

symbols.name: N_{t,n}
symbols.def: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat g_{t,n}
symbols.def: The side-specific empirical mean constructed in \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}constant\text{-}side\text{-}fit}\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}
symbols.def: The count-qualified bandwidth set constructed in \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}bandwidths}\).

symbols.name: \widehat h_{t,n}
symbols.def: The measurable bandwidth constructed in \(\mathrm{def:count\text{-}adaptive\text{-}bandwidth}\), including its empty-set fallback.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_n
symbols.def: The difference of the two count-adaptive observed-side fits constructed in \(\mathrm{def:mass\text{-}adaptive\text{-}estimator}\).

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: A nondecreasing declared common lower local-mass modulus.

symbols.name: \mathsf J_{-}
symbols.def: A declared uniform lower envelope for the thin-site packing profile.

symbols.name: \mathsf J_{+}
symbols.def: A declared uniform upper envelope for the thin-site packing profile.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:base\text{-}thickness\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \Lambda_n
symbols.def: A declared collection of exponents and lower--upper packing profiles for which the triangular union in \(\mathrm{def:triangular\text{-}profile\text{-}union}\) is nonempty.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)
symbols.type: nonempty triangular union of law classes
symbols.def: The union constructed in \(\mathrm{def:triangular\text{-}profile\text{-}union}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:isolated\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:pervasive\text{-}thinning\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: R_n
symbols.def: The minimax risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:expected\text{-}sup\text{-}risk}\).

symbols.name: r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}
symbols.def: \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}=n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\).

symbols.name: r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
symbols.def: \(r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\).

symbols.name: \rho
symbols.type: signed distance to the circular boundary
symbols.def: \(\rho(z)=\lVert z\rVert_2-1\), negative on the inside of the unit circle.

symbols.name: \mathcal T
symbols.def: \(\mathcal T=\{z\in\mathbb R^2:|\rho(z)|\le h_0\}\).

symbols.name: x_{\star}
symbols.def: A fixed point on the unit circle.

symbols.name: f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}
symbols.def: The normalized circular-tube density constructed in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\).

symbols.name: f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}
symbols.def: The normalized single-site density constructed in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\).

symbols.name: P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}
symbols.def: The zero-trace Gaussian law with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\).

symbols.name: P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}
symbols.def: The zero-trace Gaussian law with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) constructed in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\).

symbols.name: \Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}
symbols.def: A maximal \(3h\)-separated subset of the unit circle.

symbols.name: \psi_{j,h}
symbols.def: \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\) for \(x_j\in\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}\), with \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}
symbols.def: The circular pervasive tent-perturbation law constructed in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}
symbols.def: The circular isolated tent-perturbation law constructed in \(\mathrm{def:fano\text{-}tent\text{-}family}\), with \(j\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x_1=x_{\star}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf H_{\kappa}
symbols.def: The horn constructed in \(\mathrm{def:polynomial\text{-}horn}\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The exponent of an exponentially narrow horn.

symbols.name: m_{\alpha}
symbols.def: The severe modulus constructed in \(\mathrm{def:exponential\text{-}modulus}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C_n
symbols.def: A band to be derived from the handle in \(\mathrm{def:honest\text{-}band\text{-}handle}\).

symbols.name: W_n
symbols.def: \(W_n(x)=\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal C_n(x))/2\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{TV}
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{TV}(Q,Q')=\sup_E|Q(E)-Q'(E)|\).

symbols.name: \mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:modulus\text{-}profile\text{-}class}\).

assumptions.condition: \(\mathcal D_n\) consists of \(n\) independent draws induced by \(P\).

For every \(0<h\le h_0\), the maximal cardinality of an \(h\)-separated subset of \(\mathcal B\) lies in \([c_{\mathcal B}h^{-1},C_{\mathcal B}h^{-1}]\) for fixed \(0<c_{\mathcal B}\le C_{\mathcal B}<\infty\).

novel.justification: This project-specific global entropy condition is satisfied by smooth compact administrative boundaries, including the circular witnesses, and directly controls the number of boundary locations that every covering and chaining upper bound must handle; it imposes no local Ahlfors measure condition.

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(|g_{t,P}(z)-g_{t,P}(z')|\le Ld(z,z')\) for all \(z,z'\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\) with \(\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)\vee\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z',x)\le h_0\).

standard.name: Lipschitz regression smoothness on the observed design support
bounded Hölder-ball envelope for the regression trace

assumptions.condition: For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), define the one-sided restricted score measure \(\mu_{t,P}(E)=P_X(E\cap\mathcal A_t)\) on Borel sets \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^2\); there exists a single regular conditional law \(\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\) of the observed \(Y\) given \(X=z\) and, for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), a \(\mu_{t,P}\)-null set \(N_{t,P}\subseteq\mathcal X_{t,P}\) such that, simultaneously for every \(z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}\setminus N_{t,P}\) and every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}|y-g_{t,P}(z)|\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)<\infty\), \(\int_{\mathbb R}\{y-g_{t,P}(z)\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)=0\), and \(\int_{\mathbb R}\exp\{\lambda(y-g_{t,P}(z))\}\,\mathsf R_P(z,dy)\le\exp(\sigma^2\lambda^2/2)\), where \(\sigma>0\) is fixed and known.

standard.name: centered observed-side conditional sub-Gaussian regression noise; independent-error precedent only, with the restricted-kernel formulation derived here

assumptions.condition: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge c_m h^{\kappa}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: The common two-sided boundary modulus is project-specific and is realized by geographic designs whose score density vanishes polynomially with inward normal distance along an administrative boundary; Gaiffas2005Degenerate motivates polynomial design degeneracy only in a one-dimensional pointwise problem.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le C_{\mathrm{iso}}\{1+h^{-1}(u/h^2)^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(C_mh^{\kappa}\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: The envelope is realized by a single polynomial density zero on an otherwise positive tubular design and formalizes isolated geographic access bottlenecks without restricting response smoothness.
A persistent isolated thin site occurs where a smooth boundary meets one lake, pass, or data-redaction pocket, and the circular witness gives an explicit law with this property.

Boundary-wide sampling depletion arises when residence or measurement density vanishes with normal distance from an entire administrative border, and the symmetric tubular witness realizes the condition exactly.

assumptions.condition: \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(0<h\le h_0\).

novel.justification: A declared common modulus records the weakest two-sided local information available along the boundary and can be estimated from score-only pilot data in geographic designs.

assumptions.condition: \(\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\) for every \(0<h\le h_0\) and \(0\le u\le1\).

novel.justification: A lower packing envelope describes guaranteed multiplicity of sparse boundary segments and is directly realized by repeated tubular depletion.

definitions.name: nonempty triangular profile union
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)=\bigcup_{(\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\in\Lambda_n}\{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}:\mathsf J_{-}(h,u)\le\mathsf J_P(h,u)\le\mathsf J_{+}(h,u)\text{ for every }0<h\le h_0\text{ and }0\le u\le1\}\). The declared domain of \(\Lambda_n\) requires this union to be nonempty.

definitions.name: empirical one-sided counts
definitions.construction: \(N_{t,n}(x,h)=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_t,\ d(X_i,x)\le h\}\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and \(h\in\mathcal H_n\).

definitions.name: count-adaptive bandwidth
definitions.construction: For \(x\in\mathcal B\), let \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) be the numerically smallest element of \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{h\in\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)}[Lh+\sigma\sqrt{\log(e+nh^{-1})/\{N_{t,n}(x,h)\vee1\}}]\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)\ne\varnothing\), and set \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when \(\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: mass-adaptive boundary trace estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x))\) for \(x\in\mathcal B\).

definitions.name: expected-sup minimax risk
definitions.construction: For a nonempty law class \(\mathcal P\), \(R_n(\mathcal P)=\inf_{\widetilde\tau_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathbb E_P[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widetilde\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|]\), where the infimum is over estimators measurable in \(\mathcal D_n\) and the known assignment geometry.

definitions.name: explicit circular thinning witnesses
definitions.construction: Set \(\mathcal B=S^1\), \(\mathcal A_1=\{z:\rho(z)\le0\}\), and \(\mathcal A_0=\{z:\rho(z)>0\}\). On the symmetric support \(\mathcal T\), define \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)|\rho(z)|^{\kappa-2}/\int_{\mathcal T}|\rho(w)|^{\kappa-2}\,dw\) and \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}(z)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}(z)\min\{1,(d(z,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}/\int_{\mathcal T}\min\{1,(d(w,x_{\star})/h_0)^{\kappa-2}\}\,dw\). The law \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\) gives \(X\) density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), independent \(Z_0,Z_1\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\), and \(Y(t)=\sigma Z_t\); define \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\) identically with density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Both laws have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).

definitions.name: two-sided scale-dependent tent family
definitions.construction: For \(0<h\le h_0/6\), enumerate \(\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}=\{x_1,\ldots,x_{|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|}\}\), set \(\psi_{j,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_j)/h)_+\), and set \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\). Under \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), keep score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and set \(Y(1)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_1\) and \(Y(0)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(X)+\sigma Z_0\). Define \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) by the same formulas with score density \(f_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\), \(\psi_{0,h}\equiv0\), and \(\psi_{1,h}(z)=(1-d(z,x_{\star})/h)_+\). In each family, \(g_{1,P}(z)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(g_{0,P}(z)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(z)\), \(\theta_{1,P}(x)=(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\), and \(\theta_{0,P}(x)=-(Lh/4)\psi_{j,h}(x)\).

definitions.name: arbitrary-modulus optimal-recovery handle
definitions.construction: Use the count-qualified local-constant estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) on \(\mathcal H_n\), clipped to \([-2L,2L]\). Its global upper guarantee is obtained from the lower mass modulus \(m\), empirical one-sided counts \(N_{t,n}\), and global boundary entropy. Its converse uses radius-\(h/3\) Lipschitz tents at \(h\)-separated thin sites certified by \(\mathsf J_{-}\) and finite-information testing inside \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\).

definitions.name: thickness-adaptive honest-band handle
definitions.construction: Condition on the observed scores and calibrate all nonempty side averages over the finite disk-pattern family by the conditional tail radius supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:disk\text{-}pattern\text{-}sub\text{-}gaussian\text{-}control}\), whose moment-generating-function bound is derived from the centered score-conditional sub-Gaussian kernel condition; add the Lipschitz bias \(L\widehat h_{t,n}(x)\) at a positive selected count and the trace envelope \(L\) at a zero count, then difference the two sides to form \(\mathcal C_n\). For any two full observed laws, transfer simultaneous coverage between them with \(\operatorname{TV}\) to obtain the two-law expected-half-width obstruction. This handle does not perform local multiplicity calibration and does not replace full-observed-law distinguishability by score-only distinguishability.

statements.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the restriction of the observed conditional-regression equivalence class under \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\) to \(\{z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}:\inf_{x\in\mathcal B}d(z,x)<h_0\}\) has exactly one representative obeying the \(L\)-Lipschitz inequality there, namely the restriction of \(g_{t,P}\). Every \(x\in\mathcal B\) belongs to each \(\mathcal X_{t,P}\), and
\[
\theta_{t,P}(x)=\lim_{z\to x,\ z\in\mathcal X_{t,P}}g_{t,P}(z)=g_{t,P}(x)
\]
exists uniquely. Consequently the near-boundary restriction of \(g_{t,P}\), \(\theta_{t,P}\), and \(\tau_P\) are functionals of the observed law: two laws inducing the same law of \(O\) under the known assignment geometry induce the same three objects. On the intersection of \(\mathcal A_t\cap\{z:\mathbf 1\{z\in\mathcal A_1\}=t\}\) with the open \(h_0\)-tube, consistency implies that the near-boundary representative agrees, \(P_X\)-almost everywhere, with the conditional mean of \(Y(t)\) under the law normalized to that intersection whenever it has positive \(P_X\)-mass; when it has zero mass the compatibility assertion is vacuous. In particular, when the known assignment regions form the sharp partition \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), this compatibility holds \(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t}\)-almost everywhere in the open \(h_0\)-tube; this supplies the local potential-outcome interpretation without assigning a conditional mean at a null boundary point or requiring integrability of the counterfactual away from its observed side.
statements.justification: This proposition makes the target a unique observed-side trace rather than a version-dependent conditional mean at a null boundary point.
statements.gap: HahnToddVanDerKlaauw2001 identifies regression-discontinuity limits under continuity, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance studies the boundary curve; this node records identification on vanishing-support sides without assigning a conditional mean at the boundary itself.
statements.consumer: The \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflow can interpret the fitted jump as an observed-law-identified causal trace contrast even when the score has zero density on the boundary.

statements.statement: For every \(\kappa>2\), there are constants \(0<c_\kappa<C_\kappa<\infty\) such that \(c_\kappa h^{\kappa}\le\operatorname{Leb}_2(\mathsf H_{\kappa}\cap B(0,h))\le C_\kappa h^{\kappa}\) for all sufficiently small \(h\). In particular, the local-mass exponent is \(\kappa\), not \(\kappa-1\).
statements.justification: This calculation is the geometry kill test on which every polynomial-thickness rate depends.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate calibrates rates to a one-dimensional design density, while CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance does not calculate polynomial horn mass.
statements.consumer: Support diagnostics for geographic boundary designs can translate a measured horn cross-section into the correct effective-sample-size exponent.

statements.statement: Under the circular inside--outside assignment in \(\mathrm{def:circular\text{-}thinning\text{-}witnesses}\), there exist fixed \(0<c_m<C_m<\infty\) such that, for every \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) and \(P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso},0}\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\). Uniformly in \(x\in S^1\), the pervasive witness has \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides and \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp h^{-1}\). The isolated witness has \(q_{t,P}(x_{\star},h)\asymp h^{\kappa}\) on both sides, a thin arc of length \(O(h)\), \(\mathsf J_P(h,C_mh^{\kappa})\asymp1\), and the full upper profile in \(\mathrm{ass:isolated\text{-}thin\text{-}profile\text{-}upper}\). Both witnesses have \(g_{t,P}\equiv0\) and \(\theta_{t,P}\equiv0\) for \(t=0,1\).
statements.justification: The explicit circular laws prove nonemptiness and make the same-modulus, different-multiplicity comparison a legal within-model construction.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2009Uniform and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 analyze finitely many zeros in univariate regression, but neither supplies two symmetric assignment sides or a boundary-wide circular depletion witness.
statements.consumer: Simulation modules for \(\texttt{rd2d}\) can reproduce both designs from normalized score densities rather than relying on an informal horn sketch.

statements.statement: For all sufficiently small \(h\), every law in \(\{\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}}:0\le j\le|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\}\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\), the packing size satisfies \(|\Xi_h^{\mathrm{perv}}|\asymp h^{-1}\), and every pair has \(\operatorname{KL}((\mathbb P_{\kappa,j,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n},(\mathbb P_{\kappa,k,h}^{\mathrm{perv}})^{\otimes n})\le CnL^2h^{\kappa+2}/\sigma^2\). The two laws \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,0,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathbb P_{\kappa,1,h}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and their \(n\)-fold products obey the same divergence bound. At an active site, their traces are \(\theta_{1,P}(x_j)=Lh/4\), \(\theta_{0,P}(x_j)=-Lh/4\), and \(\tau_P(x_j)=Lh/2\).
statements.justification: This lemma certifies the packed lower experiment inside the same classes used by the upper bounds and states its pairwise information budget.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate uses local univariate bumps, while the present family perturbs both identified boundary sides at many separated sites without changing the common score-mass modulus.
statements.consumer: The minimax lower theorem can invoke a concrete Fano family for pervasive thinning and a concrete Le Cam pair for isolated thinning.

statements.statement: Fix \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), an assignment geometry satisfying \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\) and \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\), and constants for which \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\) are nonempty; \(\mathrm{lem:circular\text{-}witness\text{-}membership}\) supplies an explicit such specification. The two classes share the scalar lower modulus \(c_mh^{\kappa}\), but there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{iso}}\) and \(c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\le R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\). Thus no expected-sup minimax frontier is a functional of the common scalar modulus alone, and the frontier separates according to the declared thin-site multiplicity profile.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies multiplicity of thin locations, rather than local mass at the single worst point, as the missing information coordinate for uniform boundary estimation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm gives an unknown-density, spatially normalized univariate sup-norm estimator under a positive continuous design density, Gaiffas2009Uniform treats finitely many univariate density zeros, and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies known-design global \(L^2\) loss; none gives a same-modulus isolated-versus-pervasive expected-sup separation for a two-sided causal boundary.
statements.consumer: Users of the full boundary causal trace curve can distinguish one local data desert from boundary-wide depletion before interpreting a worst-case uniform rate.

statements.statement:
Suppose \(\mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\). The estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) uses neither \(\kappa\) nor the score density. Uniformly for \(\kappa\in(2,\overline\kappa]\), there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B}|\widehat\tau_n(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right]
 \le C r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}},
 \qquad
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\ge c r_{n,\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}.
\]
The fallback event obeys
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}
 P\{\exists x\in\mathcal B,\ t\in\{0,1\}:\widehat{\mathcal H}_{t,n}(x)=\varnothing\}
 \le Cn^3\exp\{-c n c_m h_0^{\kappa}\},
\]
and this event's contribution is included in the expected-risk bound.  Consequently, whenever \(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\),
\[
 R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})
 \asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})
 \asymp (\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.
\]
statements.justification: This gives a single count-qualified estimator uniformly over the maximal polynomial lower-mass class, retains the pervasive packing converse, and closes both base and pervasive minimax frontiers when the pervasive subclass is nonempty.
statements.gap: Positive-density and finitely-degenerate univariate sup-norm results do not provide a two-sided vanishing-mass boundary estimator uniform over this base class or the same-modulus pervasive converse.
statements.consumer: The \(R\), Python, and Stata \(\texttt{rd2d}\) workflows can use observed-count bandwidths throughout the base class without knowing \(\kappa\), with a specified safe fallback.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)>0\) for all \(h>0\), \(m_{\alpha}(h)\asymp h^{\alpha+1}\exp(-h^{-\alpha})\) as \(h\downarrow0\), and there exists \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that \(n m_{\alpha}(h_n)/\log n\to\infty\). Therefore a fixed exponential horn is compatible with logarithmically slow consistency and does not by itself force order-one risk.
statements.justification: This proposition removes a false early-kill premise before it contaminates the minimax theorem or the applied interpretation.
statements.gap: Gaiffas2005Degenerate obtains a logarithmic pointwise rate under severe design degeneracy; the present proposition records the corresponding boundary-modulus sanity condition without claiming a new minimax theorem.
statements.consumer: Applied analysts will not mistake an extremely thin but positive region for a formally non-estimable boundary segment.

statements.statement: For every declared pair \((m,\mathsf J_{-})\) for which \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-})\ne\varnothing\), characterize \(R_n(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-}))\) by matching same-class upper and lower bounds, construct a bandwidth rule using neither declared object, and derive a necessary-and-sufficient uniform-consistency criterion for triangular or union classes. The characterization must recover the isolated and pervasive polynomial rates and vanishing risk for every fixed positive exponential modulus represented by a nonempty named class.
statements.justification: This is the genuine open content: arbitrary irregular mass still requires conditions under which the global upper bracket and lower-packing converse match, together with an exact necessary-and-sufficient criterion for triangular or union classes.
statements.gap: The proved bracket can be strict when \(\mathsf J_{-}\) is a slack lower declaration. Gaiffas2005Degenerate covers pointwise regular and severe variation, Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm covers spatial sup-norm normalization under positive continuous univariate density, and Gaiffas2009Uniform and AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 cover univariate designs with finitely many zeros under different losses; none gives the missing exact arbitrary-modulus boundary-uniform characterization.
statements.consumer: A solved criterion would tell \(\texttt{rd2d}\) whether an observed pattern of side counts permits a uniformly consistent curve before fitting or reporting it.

statements.statement: For a declared nonempty triangular union \(\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)\), does there exist a data-measurable band \(\mathcal C_n\) such that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n)}P\{\tau_P(x)\in\mathcal C_n(x)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\}\ge1-\gamma-o(1)\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)=O(1)\)? Prove the matching honest-width lower bound: every band sequence satisfying the displayed coverage condition obeys \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(\Lambda_n),\ x\in\mathcal B}\mathbb E_P[W_n(x)]/r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}(x)\ge c\) for a universal \(c>0\). If the upper target is impossible, characterize exactly which pairs \((\kappa,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\) and \((\kappa',\mathsf J'_{-},\mathsf J'_{+})\) in \(\Lambda_n\), separated by their \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\) benchmark functions, must satisfy uniform score-law distinguishability \(\inf_{P,P'}\operatorname{TV}(P_X^{\otimes n},(P'_X)^{\otimes n})\to1\), where \(P\) and \(P'\) range over the corresponding two profile-restricted component classes.
statements.justification: The geometry-general construction gives finite-sample simultaneous coverage on every declared nonempty triangular union, and the two-full-observed-law inequality gives a geometry-general pointwise obstruction; only the matched pervasive and base global expected-sup width frontier is specialized to the certified circular polynomial classes. The uniformly local oracle-width ratio, its matching converse, and an exact score-law criterion remain unresolved.
statements.gap: Global calibration retains a logarithmic penalty where local multiplicity can be bounded, and score-law distance does not by itself control the full observed-law perturbations required by the width argument.
statements.consumer: Future work should calibrate to observable local multiplicity and determine when profile components permit compatible outcome perturbations with controlled full-law distance.

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under a known sharp bivariate boundary assignment, with score density permitted to vanish at the boundary.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O_i=(Y_i,X_i)\); potential outcomes supply the causal interpretation and only the realized outcome is observed.
sampling_model.treatment: \(T_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\in\mathcal A_1\}\), with both assignment regions and their common boundary known.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment is deterministic. Each side regression is represented on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\); consistency supplies its compatible potential-outcome interpretation, and its unique Lipschitz trace identifies \(\tau_P=\theta_{1,P}-\theta_{0,P}\). One-sided information is measured by \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Observed-side regressions are estimated by local constants with count-qualified bandwidths, a fixed measurable tie-break, and the explicit fallback \(\widehat h_{t,n}(x)=h_0\) when no bandwidth is admissible.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_n(x)=\widehat g_{1,n}(x;\widehat h_{1,n}(x))-\widehat g_{0,n}(x;\widehat h_{0,n}(x)),\quad \mathcal A_0=\mathbb R^2\setminus\mathcal A_1\Longrightarrow \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}}}\mathbb E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty\lesssim(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)},\quad \mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}}\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{base}})\asymp R_n(\mathcal P_{\kappa}^{\mathrm{perv}})\asymp(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 4--6 give regular-density uniform estimation, inference, and a distance-estimator minimax lower bound for the boundary curve.

Theorems 1--2 give spatially varying uniform regression rates under inhomogeneous one-dimensional design, and Proposition 1 shows that isolated density zeros can permit local improvement over a naive uniform normalization.
Theorems 1--2 give pointwise minimax rates under regularly and severely varying random-design density, including logarithmically slow consistency for exponential degeneracy.
The paper constructs a local-polynomial Lepski estimator adaptive to unknown pointwise design scarcity and smoothness.

The paper constructs an asymptotically sharp unknown-density estimator with a spatially varying sup-norm normalization and proposes an inhomogeneous confidence band under a positive continuous univariate design density.
The paper combines Gaussian anti-concentration, multiplier bootstrap, and data-selected resolution levels for honest adaptive bands.
Theorems 2.1--2.2 derive honest bias-aware scalar intervals and efficiency comparisons from power-renormalized bias and standard-deviation formulas.

Theorem 3.1 gives minimax lower bounds and Theorems 6.2 and 7.1 give adaptive global \(L^2\)-risk upper bounds for univariate regression with a known design density having finitely many well-separated zeros.
The paper studies minimax learning of submanifold integrals under a design density bounded away from zero, rather than boundary-indexed sup-norm traces under vanishing local mass.

tldr: The boundary target is the difference of the unique Lipschitz traces of the two observed-side regression classes on \(\operatorname{supp}(P_X|_{\mathcal A_t})\), so it is an observed-law functional even when conditional means at null boundary points are undefined. A single worst-point thickness modulus does not determine expected-sup difficulty: explicit circular designs have the same two-sided mass order \(h^{\kappa}\), but one has a single \(O(h)\)-arc data desert and the other has \(\asymp h^{-1}\) separated thin sites. The resulting nonempty classes have rates \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), respectively, and a count-qualified estimator matches the pervasive frontier without knowing \(\kappa\). The inference question asks for uniform coverage and expected half-width proportional to the explicit local benchmark \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\) over a declared nonempty triangular profile union, with total-variation distinguishability characterizing any adaptation obstruction.

project_justification.gap: Distance-based boundary-curve theory assumes positive design density. Existing random-design sup-norm theory provides unknown-density spatial normalization and inhomogeneous bands under positive continuous univariate density, while degenerate-design theory is pointwise, univariate uniform, or global \(L^2\) with finitely many zeros. These literatures do not identify how the number of thin boundary locations changes expected-sup causal-curve risk.
project_justification.niche: A common scalar local-mass modulus treats one cusp and boundary-wide depletion as the same experiment even though a supremum sees different numbers of separated hard locations.
project_justification.fill: The project defines the target through unique Lipschitz representatives on restricted-score supports, constructs explicit symmetric circular witnesses and legal two-sided tent families, proves a same-modulus rate separation, and poses both the general frontier and a quantified honest-width problem on named nonempty classes.

related_work: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026Distance is the causal and writing anchor: its Introduction motivates the full boundary curve, Theorem 4 derives the regular-density uniform stochastic term, Theorem 5 supplies Gaussian bands, and Theorem 6 gives a distance-estimator lower bound. Its density and Gram assumptions exclude the thinning regimes here, so it informs rather than supplies the proposed frontier. Gaiffas2005Degenerate, Theorems 1--2 and Section 3, motivates polynomial and severe design degeneracy in a one-dimensional pointwise model; it does not furnish the project-specific uniform two-sided boundary-mass condition, and its severe case shows that fixed exponential thinning permits logarithmically slow consistency. Gaiffas2007PointwiseAdaptive, Sections 2--4, supplies an empirical-design Lepski template at one query point. Gaiffas2007SharpSupNorm, its abstract and Section 1, constructs an unknown-design-density estimator with spatially varying sup-norm normalization and proposes an inhomogeneous confidence band, but assumes a positive continuous univariate density and supplies neither vanishing two-sided boundary mass nor a same-modulus multiplicity lower bound. Gaiffas2009Uniform, equation (2.1), Theorems 1--2, and Proposition 1, is the closest sup-loss regression comparator because it treats spatially varying rates and isolated density zeros, but it is univariate and does not provide a same-modulus two-sided boundary packing separation. AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014 studies a different global-loss problem: Section 2 assumes a known univariate design density with finitely many well-separated polynomial or exponential zeros, Theorem 3.1 gives global \(L^2\) lower bounds, and Theorems 6.2 and 7.1 give adaptive upper bounds; it does not study a boundary-indexed sup loss, pervasive thin sites, or two assignment sides. Kpotufe2011LocalDimension uses observed neighbor radii for pointwise adaptation to local ball-mass growth. The displayed global boundary-entropy condition is project-specific: every covering and chaining step in the proposed upper bounds uses only its global packing-number bound, not a local Ahlfors measure condition. ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands and ArmstrongKolesar2020Honest inform the multiplier-calibration and honest-width handles, but neither derives simultaneous local-oracle width under vanishing two-sided boundary information or the required score-law distinguishability criterion. Bull2012SelfSimilarBands concerns unknown response smoothness rather than adaptation across observable score-design profiles.
technical_internal_limitation: A scalar lower bound \(q_{t,P}(x,h)\ge m(h)\) cannot yield a sharp expected-sup lower bound without a compatible lower packing profile, and an upper theorem also needs an upper packing envelope across severity levels. The named class \(\mathcal P(m,\mathsf J_{-},\mathsf J_{+})\) makes both requirements explicit. All covering and chaining steps for the closed upper bounds use only the global packing-number control in \(\mathrm{ass:global\text{-}boundary\text{-}entropy}\); no local Ahlfors condition is invoked. For local-polynomial degree above zero, scalar mass still does not imply Gram coercivity; the closed polynomial results therefore use local constants under Lipschitz observed-side regressions.
honest_scope: The settled target is an identified contrast of unique Lipschitz observed-side traces on restricted-score supports, not a conditional expectation assigned directly at a probability-zero boundary point. The closed theorem target is the polynomial same-modulus thickness--multiplicity separation, with explicit circular nonemptiness witnesses and a matched pervasive estimator. The arbitrary-modulus minimax formula and triangular-class consistency criterion remain open. Honest thickness adaptation is posed over a declared nonempty triangular union with explicit local benchmark \(r_{n,P}^{\mathrm{loc}}\), simultaneous coverage, matching expected-width lower bound, and a total-variation distinguishability alternative. The regular positive-density regime is an external benchmark on a different model class, not a reduction of the \(\kappa>2\) pervasive theorem. A fixed positive exponential modulus remains compatible with consistency.
